title: glosa citation card
description: tier: Dr (specified; independently unreviewed). Implements FOUNDATION_v0.5.md §7.8 (Citation Integrity subsystem, generalized to distinction-grain): the Integrity Firewall's two independently-flaggable booleans (metadata_verified != claim_match_verified, NC-18 'source existence != claim support'), `identifier.kind` including BLACKBOX_NOTE (chair ruling C8), `fetch_status` as the ONE enum (chair ruling C3), and the six-value `status` enum. One card per citation USE (one source backing one exact claim at one exact passage), not one card per source document -- templates/knowledge/citation_card.yaml's own header rule. Namespace https://glosa.example/ is a placeholder. Optional, backward-compatible additions (methodology/P26_claim_evidence_theory_matrix.md, founder instruction 2026-09-25): `chaining` (backward + forward citation chaining for the source, recorded once per source on one card) and `audit` (claim-level citation audit of the manuscript sentence(s) that use this card: VERIFIED | RELAYED | OVERREACH).

claim_match_verified.description: NC-18, non-collapsible boundary: 'source existence != claim support'. Never inferred from metadata_verified.

fetched_from_url.description: REQUIRED when fetch_status == FETCHED (kernel rule 17, founder ruling 2026-09-04 BBL-2026-09-04-100): the exact link the text was read from (open-access page, PMC/Europe PMC mirror, Wayback snapshot, arXiv html, or file path for a local full text). Never a citation from memory.

line_or_paragraph.description: Line number / paragraph index / section anchor within the fetched text where exact_passage starts (kernel rule 17). Together with page_or_locator this is the 'page and line'.

chaining.description: P26 item (d): backward chaining (this source's own reference list) and forward chaining (works citing this source), each link screened. Optional. Recorded ONCE per source document -- on the lowest-id card for that source; other cards for the same source leave it absent (one-fact-one-home; a citation card is per USE, chaining is per SOURCE). Forward chaining is a readout of one moment: `as_of` + `route` say which index was asked and when.

route.description: How the links were obtained, e.g. 'reference list read in full' (backward) or the name of a public citation index queried (forward). Never a private-shelf identifier (P13 research-stack boundary).

audit.description: P26 item (e): claim-level citation audit, sentence by sentence. Distinct from claim_match_verified: claim_match_verified asks whether exact_passage supports claim_ref as carded; audit asks whether the manuscript sentence(s) citing this card stay within that support. VERIFIED = checker read the source passage and the sentence claims no more than it supports; RELAYED = the sentence rests on a source the checker has not read directly (secondary or remembered; FC-S14-1 forbids this from backing a published claim); OVERREACH = the passage was read and the sentence claims more than it supports. Absent = not yet audited. checked_by must not be the sentence's maker (AGENTS.md rule 3).

sentence_refs.description: Manuscript locators (section/paragraph/sentence) of the audited sentence(s).

citation_card_ref.description: id of the citation card opened for this linked work, if it was carried into the review.

allOf.description: exact_passage is required whenever claim_match_verified is true (S8 template rule) -- never a paraphrase substituting for the actual check.
status VERIFIED requires both booleans true (Integrity Firewall).
audit.status VERIFIED requires claim_match_verified true: a sentence cannot be audited as supported by a passage whose claim match is itself unverified.
